patch.value: Release 2026.11.15 changelog heading drifts after rollover publication

Baseline origin/main fails npm run changelog:check. CHANGELOG.md says 2026.11.15 - 2026-11-15, while tag v2026.11.15 points at the November 16 release commit. The pinned generator derives the tagged heading from commit time, regenerating 2026-11-16. Confirmed on unchanged origin/main while fixing #290.
Resolve the existing tagged release-heading date policy mismatch; npm run changelog:check and release date checks agree before and after rollover without changing historical tags.

Regeneration changes only the first heading date from 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-16. No historical tags or changelog content were changed for #290.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: 2026-11-16 20:0xZ (orchestrator): root cause filed as unbraind/pm-ops#292. v2026.11.15 was prepared and tagged on 11-16, prepare rendered the heading from the version (2026-11-15), and after tagging pm-changelog uses the real tag date (2026-11-16, by design per pm-changelog#120). Regenerated CHANGELOG.md in PR #291 so 'npm run changelog:check' passes on this branch (exit 0); main stays red until #291 or another regeneration merges.

value.author: pi-ops-292
value.text:
Root cause (issue #292): prepare renders the pending version's heading with --date-from-version, so a resumed candidate (version day before today) is stamped with its version day. The release step then tags it today; pm-changelog by design derives a tagged window's heading from the tag commit date (pm-changelog#120), so post-tag regeneration on unchanged main renders a different day and changelog:check is red on main. The release PR's own CI passes (candidate still untagged), so the failure only appears after the merge.

Design: use the generator's existing --date-fallback flag (applies only while no release tag exists; ignored once the tag exists, so it matches post-tag invocations byte-for-byte). decideDailyRelease now outputs heading_date: today in RELEASE_TIMEZONE, padded ISO, when the version's calendar day is before today; empty for a same-day release, which is therefore unchanged. The 'Generate changelog and release notes' step, in the same in-place package.json policy rewrite that already appends --include-empty, swaps --date-from-version for --date-fallback <heading_date> in the three changelog scripts when resumed, refreshes a stale pin when a candidate is re-prepared on a later day, and restores --date-from-version when the pending version is current again. The release commit carries the pinned spelling, so the release PR's CI (untagged candidate), prepare's nested release:check and post-tag checks on main all regenerate the same bytes with no follow-up regeneration. The date verifier accepts a pinned --date-fallback day (explicit ISO day only) as an equally clock-free alternative to --date-from-version. Rust/justfile releases (CHANGELOG_DATE derived from the tag name) keep their own spelling and are not touched.

The one red linked-test record for 'npm test' is an environment interaction, not a regression: under pm test --run's schema sandbox, the untouched verify-lifecycle-policy non-vacuity test spawns the pinned pm binary in a scratch project and inherits the harness environment, so its scratch init does not create schema/policies.json (ENOENT); the same file passes standalone in 22/22 tests, and the full suite passes outside the sandbox. Contract test 'prepare commits the heading its tag produces, for same-day and resumed releases' runs the real workflow step script over a fixture tracker for both scenarios and proves prepare bytes == post-tag regeneration, the release PR's untagged gate passes, and the pinned spelling is restored by the next current release.

value.author: pi-ops-292
value.text: Delivered in PR #295 (branch fix/resumed-release-heading-date, head 76064a0). Open risks: (1) the item file and its history are introduced to main by this PR because they currently live only on the open pending-version branch that first filed them; a merge-order conflict there is expected and trivial. (2) The workflow change reaches fleet callers only when they pin a pm-ops release that contains it. (3) Rust/justfile repos derive CHANGELOG_DATE from the tag name and would show the same resumed-day drift; that path is untouched here and needs its own follow-up. (4) A resumed release still assumes the tag lands the same day the candidate is prepared; a merge crossing midnight reintroduces one day of drift, as before.

value.author: pi-claude
value.text:
Round on the open review thread for scripts/verify-release-changelog-date.ts (line 55) plus the origin/main merge.

Merge: merged origin/main (fb68e7d) into fix/resumed-release-heading-date. The add/add conflicts on the tracker item (.toon) and its history stream resolved to this branch's side after verifying with cmp that main's 4-line history is a byte-exact prefix of this branch's 39-line history; no history line was edited or reordered. The auto-merged .github/workflows/daily-release.yml, daily-release.ts and test/daily-release.test.ts were reviewed: main's registry-held pending-version skip and the restart-prepare wiring are intact and compose with this branch's heading policy. pm health --strict-exit initially failed with merge_driver_configuration_drift (the 5 merge-driver keys pointed at a foreign pm-cli); rerunning merge install through the repository-pinned ./node_modules/.bin/pm (the same binary CI Deep uses) repointed them at the repository's pinned dependency and pm health --strict-exit then exits 0 with only advisory warnings (stale/unowned/idle in-progress items).

Fix: the pinned --date-fallback day is now validated against the real calendar, not just its shape. FALLBACK_DATE_PATTERN captures the day and a new isRealCalendarDay helper round-trips the components through UTC (setUTCFullYear, avoiding the 1900s two-digit-year mapping in Date.UTC) and compares them back, so 2026-02-30, 2026-13-01, 2026-04-31 and the non-leap 2026-02-29 are rejected in both the space and '=' spellings while the leap-year 2028-02-29 stays accepted; the audit reports a distinct 'day does not exist on the calendar' defect for a shape-correct impossible day.

dist/: no rebuild committed. The repository's only dist-parity enforcement is the daily-release workflow's 'Pack verified release' step (git diff --exit-code and the dist/ porcelain check after the release's own build), which runs on main's release candidate, not on a PR branch; PR CI rebuilds before testing and never compares against the committed build, so no PR-branch gate requires it. The build artifacts produced by running the coverage gate were reverted. Tracked dist/ still predates this branch's daily-release.ts helpers; follow-up item ops-b2bs records that the first post-merge release pack step would fail until dist is rebuilt on main.
